transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what brings me in is… after I do it, after I eat like that, I’m left sitting there looking at all the empty containers. And I just feel disgusted with myself. Like I’m not the steady, in-control man I’ve always tried to be.
How often do these eating episodes happen?
Since I’ve been home with this back injury, it’s been several nights most weeks. I honestly can’t think of a week in the last three months where it didn’t happen at least once.
Do you ever try to make up for these eating episodes by doing something to compensate, like exercising or vomiting?
I don’t really know. I mean, I feel bad afterward, but I’m not sure what you mean by “make up for it.”
Do you ever vomit after one of these eating episodes?
No… I don’t make myself throw up after. I just feel awful and sit with it, but vomiting isn’t something I do.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during these episodes?
No, not really. Once I start, it’s like whatever discipline I usually have just shuts off. I’ll be telling myself, “Magin, put the fork down,” but my hand still keeps going back for more.
Do you usually feel guilty after these eating episodes?

Yes. I usually feel really guilty afterward. I’ll be sitting there looking at the empty containers, and I just feel disgusted with myself… like I’m not the steady, in-control man I’ve always tried to be.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're eating a lot more food than you normally would in a similar period of time?

Yes. It’s a lot more than I’d normally eat. Like some evenings I’ll heat up what I tell myself is just one bowl of pozole, and then before I know it I’ve gone through most of the pot… plus a couple tamales, chips, whatever leftovers are there. It’s like I’m eating enough for a whole crew, not just me.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during these episodes?

Yes. I eat fast, really fast. It’s like I’m on a tight delivery schedule or something, just shoveling it in. Half the time I’m barely tasting it, and sometimes I notice I’m breathing hard because I haven’t even slowed down.
Do you usually eat during these episodes when you're alone?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to whether I’m always alone when it happens. I think… sometimes I just don’t want anyone noticing, but I can’t say for sure.
Have these episodes of eating like this been happening for more than three months?
It’s been about three months, yeah. It started after I strained my back and got taken off the road, and it’s been happening since then.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these episodes?
Yes. Once I start, it feels like whatever self-control I usually have just shuts off. I’ll be telling myself, Magin, put the fork down, stop now, but my hand keeps going back for more anyway.
Do you feel like you're eating in response to an emotional state, such as stress or anxiety, when these episodes happen?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like that. Sometimes I guess I’m wound up or bothered, but I can’t say for sure that’s what sets it off.
Do you think your eating episodes are usually triggered by feelings of stress, anxiety, or other emotions?
I don’t really know. I haven’t been able to pin it down to stress or anxiety, exactly. Sometimes I might be upset or on edge, but other times it just happens and I can’t tell what started it.
Do you think you might be eating like this when you're bored, now that you're not working due to your back injury?
I’m not sure. I guess being home more could be part of it, but I haven’t really noticed it happening just because I’m bored. I can’t say that’s the reason.
Do you feel like you have no control over what or how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yeah… during those times it really does feel like I don’t have control. Once I start, it’s like the discipline I used to have just shuts off. I’ll even be telling myself, “Magin, put the fork down,” but my hand still keeps going back for more.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself from continuing to eat once you've started eating during these episodes?

Yes. Once I’ve started, it’s like I can’t make myself stop. I’ll be thinking, Magin, put the fork down, but my hand just keeps going back for more anyway. It’s like the discipline I used to have just shuts off.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself from continuing to eat once you've started eating during these episodes, because you feel like something is driving you to keep eating?

Yeah, that’s pretty much it. Once I start, it feels like whatever discipline I used to have just shuts off. I’ll be telling myself, Magin, put the fork down, but my hand keeps going back for more anyway.
Are these eating episodes affecting your daily activities or relationships in any way?
Yeah, it has. I’ve started avoiding check-in calls from the drivers I’m supposed to be mentoring. I just feel ashamed, like I don’t want them hearing how far off my routine I’ve gotten.
Do you feel like you're eating during these episodes without being able to restrain yourself?
Yes. I mean, I know I should stop, and I’m telling myself to stop, but once I’ve started it feels like that discipline I had on the road just shuts off. My hand just keeps going back for more.
